findings.body: The variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner evaluates to false for team admins because `&&` requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to be truthy; the admin receives a FORBIDDEN error and cannot add guests despite the intended admin-or-owner semantics.
findings.failure_mode: Team admins are incorrectly denied access to the new add-guests feature.
findings.impact: The variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner evaluates to false for team admins because `&&` requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to be truthy; the admin receives a FORBIDDEN error and cannot add guests despite the intended admin-or-owner semantics.
findings.root_cause: Logical AND used where OR was intended between the two role checks, contradicting the variable name and intended authorization semantics.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `||` (or simply the isTeamAdmin result, which already accepts ADMIN or OWNER roles) instead of `&&`.
findings.title: Permission check requires team ADMIN AND OWNER instead of admin-or-owner
findings.trigger: A user with team role ADMIN (but not OWNER), who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee, calls the addGuests mutation for a team booking.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 46-48 show `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner calls. isTeamAdmin already returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER roles (context L264-283), so the variable name 'isTeamAdminOrOwner' contradicts the `&&` logic which requires both conditions. A team admin who is not owner would fail this check and receive FORBIDDEN.

raw_findings.body: The variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner evaluates to false for team admins because `&&` requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to be truthy; the admin receives a FORBIDDEN error and cannot add guests despite the intended admin-or-owner semantics.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Team admins are incorrectly denied access to the new add-guests feature.
raw_findings.impact: The variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner evaluates to false for team admins because `&&` requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to be truthy; the admin receives a FORBIDDEN error and cannot add guests despite the intended admin-or-owner semantics.
raw_findings.root_cause: Logical AND used where OR was intended between the two role checks, contradicting the variable name and intended authorization semantics.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `||` (or simply the isTeamAdmin result, which already accepts ADMIN or OWNER roles) instead of `&&`.
raw_findings.title: Permission check requires team ADMIN AND OWNER instead of admin-or-owner
raw_findings.trigger: A user with team role ADMIN (but not OWNER), who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee, calls the addGuests mutation for a team booking.

raw_findings.body: updateCalendarAttendees runs with the caller's (often empty or unrelated) credentials, so the organizer's calendar/video event is never updated with the new guests; guests are saved in the DB but the external calendar invite stays stale.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent failure to propagate new guests to the connected calendar when an attendee or team admin adds them.
raw_findings.impact: updateCalendarAttendees runs with the caller's (often empty or unrelated) credentials, so the organizer's calendar/video event is never updated with the new guests; guests are saved in the DB but the external calendar invite stays stale.
raw_findings.root_cause: Handler unconditionally uses the session user's credentials for calendar sync while allowing non-organizer callers.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When the caller is not the organizer, construct EventManager from the booking owner's credentials (booking.user.credentials, already included in the query) or the destination calendar's credential.
raw_findings.title: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
raw_findings.trigger: An attendee or team admin (not the booking organizer) invokes addGuests; the handler builds EventManager from ctx.user's credentials even though the booking query already fetched booking.user.credentials.

raw_findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is compared verbatim, so any mixed-case variant bypasses the guest email blacklist and gets added and emailed, unlike the existing checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked behavior.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Blacklisted emails are added as guests and receive booking emails.
raw_findings.impact: The blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is compared verbatim, so any mixed-case variant bypasses the guest email blacklist and gets added and emailed, unlike the existing checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked behavior.
raw_findings.root_cause: Asymmetric normalization: only the env-derived blacklist is lowercased, not the user-supplied guest emails.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Lowercase the guest email before the includes() comparison: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.
raw_findings.title: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is case-sensitive on the guest side and can be bypassed
raw_findings.trigger: A caller submits a blacklisted address with different casing (e.g. "Blocked@Example.com" when BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains "blocked@example.com").

raw_findings.body: createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows for the same email on one booking, producing duplicate emails and corrupt attendee data; uniqueness is only enforced client-side in AddGuestsDialog.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate attendee records created for a booking from a single malformed request.
raw_findings.impact: createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows for the same email on one booking, producing duplicate emails and corrupt attendee data; uniqueness is only enforced client-side in AddGuestsDialog.
raw_findings.root_cause: Uniqueness validation exists only in the client-side dialog schema, not in the server input schema or handler.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add the same uniqueness refine to ZAddGuestsInputSchema (or dedupe the guests array in the handler before createMany).
raw_findings.title: Server schema/handler allow duplicate guest emails within a single request
raw_findings.trigger: A client (or direct tRPC/API caller bypassing the dialog's client-side refine) sends guests: ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]; the handler's uniqueGuests filter only deduplicates against existing attendees, not within the input array.

raw_findings.body: In sendAddGuestsEmails, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` matches the pre-existing attendee, so that attendee receives the "your event has been scheduled" AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the intended "guests added" notification.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Wrong email template sent to existing attendees when the request repeats their address.
raw_findings.impact: In sendAddGuestsEmails, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` matches the pre-existing attendee, so that attendee receives the "your event has been scheduled" AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the intended "guests added" notification.
raw_findings.root_cause: The email dispatch uses the unfiltered request payload to classify recipients as new vs existing attendees.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `uniqueGuests` (the actually-added set) to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the raw `guests` input.

validated_findings.body: The variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner evaluates to false for team admins because `&&` requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to be truthy; the admin receives a FORBIDDEN error and cannot add guests despite the intended admin-or-owner semantics.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Team admins are incorrectly denied access to the new add-guests feature.
validated_findings.impact: The variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner evaluates to false for team admins because `&&` requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to be truthy; the admin receives a FORBIDDEN error and cannot add guests despite the intended admin-or-owner semantics.
validated_findings.root_cause: Logical AND used where OR was intended between the two role checks, contradicting the variable name and intended authorization semantics.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `||` (or simply the isTeamAdmin result, which already accepts ADMIN or OWNER roles) instead of `&&`.
validated_findings.title: Permission check requires team ADMIN AND OWNER instead of admin-or-owner
validated_findings.trigger: A user with team role ADMIN (but not OWNER), who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee, calls the addGuests mutation for a team booking.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 46-48 show `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner calls. isTeamAdmin already returns truthy for ADMIN or OWNER roles (context L264-283), so the variable name 'isTeamAdminOrOwner' contradicts the `&&` logic which requires both conditions. A team admin who is not owner would fail this check and receive FORBIDDEN.

validated_findings.body: updateCalendarAttendees runs with the caller's (often empty or unrelated) credentials, so the organizer's calendar/video event is never updated with the new guests; guests are saved in the DB but the external calendar invite stays stale.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silent failure to propagate new guests to the connected calendar when an attendee or team admin adds them.
validated_findings.impact: updateCalendarAttendees runs with the caller's (often empty or unrelated) credentials, so the organizer's calendar/video event is never updated with the new guests; guests are saved in the DB but the external calendar invite stays stale.
validated_findings.root_cause: Handler unconditionally uses the session user's credentials for calendar sync while allowing non-organizer callers.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: When the caller is not the organizer, construct EventManager from the booking owner's credentials (booking.user.credentials, already included in the query) or the destination calendar's credential.
validated_findings.title: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
validated_findings.trigger: An attendee or team admin (not the booking organizer) invokes addGuests; the handler builds EventManager from ctx.user's credentials even though the booking query already fetched booking.user.credentials.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 158-163 show credentials fetched via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), not from booking.user.credentials (which is already included per lines 35-39). When a non-organizer (attendee or team admin) calls addGuests, their credentials are used for EventManager, so updateCalendarAttendees operates on wrong credentials.

validated_findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is compared verbatim, so any mixed-case variant bypasses the guest email blacklist and gets added and emailed, unlike the existing checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked behavior.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Blacklisted emails are added as guests and receive booking emails.
validated_findings.impact: The blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is compared verbatim, so any mixed-case variant bypasses the guest email blacklist and gets added and emailed, unlike the existing checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked behavior.
validated_findings.root_cause: Asymmetric normalization: only the env-derived blacklist is lowercased, not the user-supplied guest emails.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Lowercase the guest email before the includes() comparison: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.
validated_findings.title: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is case-sensitive on the guest side and can be bypassed
validated_findings.trigger: A caller submits a blacklisted address with different casing (e.g. "Blocked@Example.com" when BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains "blocked@example.com").
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 70-77 show blacklistedGuestEmails lowercased but guest compared verbatim via includes(guest). Mixed-case input bypasses the blacklist. Other usages in codebase (handleNewBooking.ts) also lowercase the blacklist but the comparison pattern varies.

validated_findings.body: createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows for the same email on one booking, producing duplicate emails and corrupt attendee data; uniqueness is only enforced client-side in AddGuestsDialog.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate attendee records created for a booking from a single malformed request.
validated_findings.impact: createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows for the same email on one booking, producing duplicate emails and corrupt attendee data; uniqueness is only enforced client-side in AddGuestsDialog.
validated_findings.root_cause: Uniqueness validation exists only in the client-side dialog schema, not in the server input schema or handler.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add the same uniqueness refine to ZAddGuestsInputSchema (or dedupe the guests array in the handler before createMany).
validated_findings.title: Server schema/handler allow duplicate guest emails within a single request
validated_findings.trigger: A client (or direct tRPC/API caller bypassing the dialog's client-side refine) sends guests: ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]; the handler's uniqueGuests filter only deduplicates against existing attendees, not within the input array.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 5 shows server schema z.array(z.string().email()) without uniqueness refine. Handler's uniqueGuests filter (lines 74-78) only dedupes against existing attendees, not within the input array itself. Duplicate emails in a single request would create duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

validated_findings.body: In sendAddGuestsEmails, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` matches the pre-existing attendee, so that attendee receives the "your event has been scheduled" AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the intended "guests added" notification.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Wrong email template sent to existing attendees when the request repeats their address.
validated_findings.impact: In sendAddGuestsEmails, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` matches the pre-existing attendee, so that attendee receives the "your event has been scheduled" AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the intended "guests added" notification.
validated_findings.root_cause: The email dispatch uses the unfiltered request payload to classify recipients as new vs existing attendees.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `uniqueGuests` (the actually-added set) to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the raw `guests` input.
validated_findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw input `guests` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
validated_findings.trigger: The input guests array includes an email that is already an attendee (filtered out of uniqueGuests) alongside at least one genuinely new guest, so the mutation proceeds.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 168 passes raw `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails, not `uniqueGuests`. In sendAddGuestsEmails (line 541), newGuests.includes(attendee.email) would match pre-existing attendees if their email was in the original input, sending them AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.

validated_findings.body: Organizer, team member, and attendee emails are sent unconditionally, overriding the event type's disable-standard-emails configuration that sibling flows respect.
validated_findings.evidence: export const sendAddGuestsEmails = async (calEvent: CalendarEvent, newGuests: string[]) => {
validated_findings.failure_mode: Emails delivered to recipients who configured them off, an unexpected behavior change for such event types.
validated_findings.impact: Organizer, team member, and attendee emails are sent unconditionally, overriding the event type's disable-standard-emails configuration that sibling flows respect.
validated_findings.root_cause: New email-manager function omits the eventTypeMetadata gating pattern used by the adjacent sendLocationChangeEmails.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Accept eventTypeMetadata (available on booking.eventType in the handler) and gate organizer/attendee sends with eventTypeDisableHostEmail / eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, mirroring sendLocationChangeEmails.
validated_findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable settings unlike sendLocationChangeEmails
validated_findings.trigger: Guests are added to a booking whose event type metadata disables attendee or host emails (the same metadata that sendLocationChangeEmails checks via eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail directly above this function).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 525-537 show sendAddGuestsEmails sends emails unconditionally without checking eventTypeMetadata for disable flags, unlike adjacent sendLocationChangeEmails (lines 515-521) which checks eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. This is a behavioral inconsistency introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: `message` is a template literal and therefore always truthy, so the `t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never execute, and the user sees a toast beginning with "undefined: ".
validated_findings.failure_mode: Confusing "undefined: ..." error toast shown to users; intended fallback string is unreachable.
validated_findings.impact: `message` is a template literal and therefore always truthy, so the `t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never execute, and the user sees a toast beginning with "undefined: ".
validated_findings.root_cause: Truthiness fallback applied to a template literal that is never empty.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Build the message conditionally, e.g. `const message = err.data?.code ? \`${err.data.code}: ${t(err.message)}\` : t("unable_to_add_guests");`.
validated_findings.title: Error toast fallback is dead code and can render "undefined:" prefix
validated_findings.trigger: The addGuests mutation fails with an error lacking data.code (e.g. a network/transport error).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 43-44 show template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` which is always a non-empty string (truthy), making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback unreachable. When err.data?.code is undefined, user sees 'undefined: ...' prefix.

validated_findings.body: multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail persist, so the reopened dialog shows stale email entries and/or a stale "Emails must be unique and valid" error, unlike the Cancel button path which resets both.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent UI state on reopen depending on how the dialog was dismissed.
validated_findings.impact: multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail persist, so the reopened dialog shows stale email entries and/or a stale "Emails must be unique and valid" error, unlike the Cancel button path which resets both.
validated_findings.root_cause: State reset logic exists only in the Cancel button onClick, not in the dialog's onOpenChange close path.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Reset multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail in a single close handler used by both onOpenChange(false) and the Cancel button.
validated_findings.title: Dialog state (emails, invalid flag) not reset when closed via overlay/onOpenChange
validated_findings.trigger: User enters emails (or triggers the invalid-email error), then closes the dialog by clicking the overlay or pressing Escape (onOpenChange path) instead of the Cancel button, then reopens it.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 61 shows Dialog with onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}. State reset (setMultiEmailValue, setIsInvalidEmail) only occurs in Cancel button onClick (not shown but implied by onSuccess at line 39). Closing via overlay/Escape triggers onOpenChange but doesn't reset state, unlike Cancel path.

validated_findings.body: The organizer receives this email with a different sender display name than every other OrganizerScheduledEmail-derived email (which use EMAIL_FROM_NAME), breaking sender-name consistency and configured branding.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent, non-configurable sender name for this one email type.
validated_findings.impact: The organizer receives this email with a different sender display name than every other OrganizerScheduledEmail-derived email (which use EMAIL_FROM_NAME), breaking sender-name consistency and configured branding.
validated_findings.root_cause: New template copied an outdated from-header pattern instead of following the base class's EMAIL_FROM_NAME convention.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use EMAIL_FROM_NAME from @calcom/lib/constants like the parent OrganizerScheduledEmail does.
validated_findings.title: Organizer add-guests email uses APP_NAME as from-name, diverging from base class EMAIL_FROM_NAME
validated_findings.trigger: An add-guests organizer email is sent on a self-hosted instance where EMAIL_FROM_NAME is customized to differ from APP_NAME.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Candidate claims APP_NAME differs from EMAIL_FROM_NAME, but this is a stylistic/consistency concern. The parent class OrganizerScheduledEmail uses EMAIL_FROM_NAME (context L47), but the new class intentionally overrides getNodeMailerPayload. This is a design choice, not a defect with concrete impact.
